title: 식당 예약 전화: 언제, 몇 분이세요?
objective: Understand and answer the staff's polite -(으)세요 questions to book a table.
summary: Practice a short phone call to book a table.
setting: A customer calls a restaurant to book a table for Saturday evening.

task.title: Book a table by phone
task.line: Read each item, then write or choose the Korean answer.

words.exampleMeaning: It's my friend's birthday, so I booked a restaurant.

words.meaning: do you come? (a polite question from 오다 + -세요). After a stem that ends in a consonant, use -으세요: 앉다 → 앉으세요.
words.exampleMeaning: What time are you coming tomorrow?

words.meaning: how many people (polite; staff use this when they talk to guests)
people (the counter you use for yourself and your group)
words.exampleMeaning: Do you have a table for five?

words.meaning: name (polite word; staff use it when they ask for your name)

dialogue.meaning: Hello. I'd like to make a reservation.
How many people will there be?
Four people. Do you have a table?
Yes, we can do that. May I have your name?
It's Michael. My phone number is 010-1234-5678.

exercises: Change the verb in brackets to the polite -(으)세요 form: ① 내일 몇 시에 (가다)? ② 여기 (앉다). ③ 잠깐만 (기다리다).
Choose the right word: ① 직원: 오늘 몇 (분 / 명) 오세요? ② 손님: 여섯 (분 / 명)이에요.
Put the words in order to make one sentence: 싶어요 / 점심을 / 예약하고 / 금요일
Answer in Korean as the customer: ① 직원: 언제 오세요? (Friday, 6 p.m.) ② 직원: 성함이 어떻게 되세요? (Your name is Anna.)
answers: ① 가세요 ② 앉으세요 ③ 기다리세요
① 금요일 저녁 여섯 시요. (금요일 오후 여섯 시요. / 금요일 저녁 여섯 시에 가요.) ② 안나예요. (안나입니다.)
